solution.what: ANA PDF of 558-1-31 downloaded (6.3 MB, 98 images); images 41-42 extracted at their embedded size.
Catalogue vetting record of 28 Oct 2026 and one web search: no edition or decipherment found.
Cipher runs transcribed twice from crops without the key; R02, R10 and R12 settled on 6x-8x crops.

Crib 'ocupacion' for run R05 (before the clear 'de Grande') gave seven values; an alphabetical-order rule fitted three consonant orders, all frozen before any other run was decrypted (key_candidates.tsv).

Held-out: the other 11 runs (76 groups). Whole-run lexicon measure: candidate A 64.5%, B 60.5%, C 31.6%; 1,000 shuffled keys keeping the crib values: mean 9.1%, max 44.7%. By hand, A gives contrata, pesos, Olinda (twice), Paulino, declaracon, de, ministerial and ocupagion; B and C give che for de. A frozen as the key.

Letter read with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py passes. Dan's reading checker: clean share 0.536 (reading, 15 of 28 sentences), 0.59 (translation, 23 of 39 sentences; 0.561, 23 of 41, after the notes were reworded on 13 Nov).

Blind review by an AI language-model agent that did not take part in the solve: 64 group occurrences in 9 runs or part-runs re-read on the images, 64 of 64 agree with the transcription; own decryption code gives the same output; held-out figures reproduced; 13 of 15 sentences hold, 1 borderline, 1 fails. State read in part, grade B.

Integration check (13 Nov 2026): check_marks.py and heldout.py re-run with the repo lexicon (candidate A 49/76 groups, 64.5%; shuffles mean 9.1%, max 44.7%, none at or above A). Strict share 9 of 21 items = 42.9% (the 7 lone numbers and the sign count as holes); the text-level read_share is set to that figure (it was 0.643, the share of the 14 letter-table words only). Read in part. The other letters of 558-1-31 were not paged for more cipher in this table: workable, so the target stays in progress and has no page.

texts.label: 13 Feb 1850, ANA-AHRP-PY-558-1-31 item 13, sheets 586-587
texts.summary: Varela acknowledges the consul's notes of 17 October and 21 November 1849 with the newspapers, news of an English contract and of Montevideo (partly unread), and that 'that one' received the pesos. Hopkins has arrived with the consul's letter of 12 November. The President does not see why news of a concentration should please [25], unless [25] dreams of the occupation of [Rio] Grande. He has seen in print the business of Olinda with [1]; it is strange that Paulino should feel embarrassed by Olinda's declaration to [1] about the occupation of [Rio] Grande; he is tainted with ministerial perfidy. The contributor identifies Olinda and Paulino as very likely the Brazilian foreign ministers of 1849-50.
texts.note: Cipher words 14: 9 verbatim from the signs (64.3%), 2 with a marked repair, 0 from a gloss, 3 holes; 7 occurrences of lone numbers or signs (25 twice, 1 twice, 116, 98, barred circle; 5 distinct) not identified. Reading checker clean share 0.536 (15 of 28 sentences); translation 0.561 (23 of 41).

reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the translation: 13 of 15 sentences hold with at most about one hole in ten words, 1 is borderline and the closing sentence fails; the cipher runs R02, R03 and the R12 tail are open and the lone numbers 25, 1, 116, 98 and the barred-circle sign are unidentified. A sign check of 64 group occurrences on the images agreed with the transcription.

98 is outside the table; 'de lg' not read; the last group has a line through it.
